A box of meaningful traditions

◆

Samriddhi Box is a carefully put together set of four items traditionally associated with prosperity, abundance and new beginnings. It comes in a gold-rimmed keepsake tin, made to be displayed, gifted and treasured.

ITEM 1 OF 4

Silver Fish

In many Indian traditions the fish is an auspicious symbol of abundance, good fortune and graceful movement through life. Fine scales, a flowing tail and a sculpted fin make it a lovely reminder to keep near your finances.

ASSOCIATED WITHAbundance
Good fortune
Graceful flow
WHERE TO KEEPLocker
Cash counter
ITEM 2 OF 4

Pyrite Stone

Known for its warm, golden shimmer, pyrite is associated in crystal traditions with confidence, opportunity and abundance. Its sparkling crystal surface makes each stone a striking keepsake.

ASSOCIATED WITHConfidence
Opportunity
Abundance
WHERE TO KEEPCash counter
Cashflow place

Each stone is naturally formed, so shape and sparkle vary slightly.

ITEM 3 OF 4

Zubu Coin

A smooth green stone engraved in gold with the numbers 808, 520 and 741 inside a circle. Many people use it as a focal point for setting intentions for abundance and positive change.

ASSOCIATED WITHProsperity
Intention
Focus
WHERE TO KEEPWallet
Cash drawer

Interpretations vary by tradition and practitioner.

ITEM 4 OF 4

Kuber Kunji

In Indian tradition Lord Kuber is the guardian of wealth, and a key is a classic symbol of unlocking doors to new opportunities. The golden key has an ornate crest with a star motif at its centre.

ASSOCIATED WITHNew beginnings
Opportunity
Auspiciousness
WHERE TO KEEPN–NE direction
Between 0° and 60°
